ai.chat.title: AI assistant
ai.chat.quick_question: Please analyze this capture comprehensively: is there any anomaly, what are the possible causes, and is optimization needed?
ai.chat.quick.smoothness: Analyze smoothness in this capture: frame rate, frame time, stutters and 1% Low. Answer only from the available evidence and state clearly when nothing is abnormal.
ai.chat.quick.hardware: Analyze hardware load in this capture: CPU, GPU, memory and VRAM. If telemetry is missing, say that the data is insufficient.
ai.chat.quick.network: Analyze network performance in this capture: latency, jitter, timeouts and coverage. When no network data exists, do not call the network normal or abnormal.
ai.chat.quick.optimization: Based on the actual evidence in this capture, is optimization needed? If no clear problem exists, say no optimization is needed and do not invent problems.

analysis.glossary.fps.description: Frames per second. Higher is smoother, but an average can hide short slow moments.
analysis.glossary.one_percent_low.descri: The average FPS of the slowest 1% of frames. A low value means there are occasional very slow frames.
analysis.glossary.p99.description: The frame time that 99% of frames are faster than. It shows how bad the slowest moments are.
analysis.glossary.frame_time.description: How long one frame took, in milliseconds. Lower is better.
analysis.glossary.qpc.description: A high-resolution Windows timer. LagLens uses it to line up frame times with hardware samples more accurately.
analysis.glossary.telemetry.description: Optional CPU, GPU and RAM samples recorded during a capture. Without it, hardware readings cannot be tied to specific frames.

analysis.diagnostics.guide.title: Step-by-step troubleshooting
analysis.diagnostics.guide.note: Change only one variable at a time and repeat the same game scene. This guide does not modify any game, driver or Windows setting.
analysis.diagnostics.guide.empty: Select a finding to see its step-by-step guide.
analysis.diagnostics.guide.cpu.step1: Keep the game scene and graphics settings fixed; close one high-CPU background app.
analysis.diagnostics.guide.cpu.step2: Capture the same scene again with QPC timebase and a complete telemetry sidecar.
analysis.diagnostics.guide.cpu.step3: Compare CPUBusy, CPUWait and local dynamic anomalies with the previous run.
analysis.diagnostics.guide.cpu.step4: If nothing improves, restore that app and change only one CPU-related game setting; repeat.
analysis.diagnostics.guide.gpu.step1: Keep CPU/background settings fixed; lower one GPU setting such as resolution or graphics preset.
analysis.diagnostics.guide.gpu.step2: Capture the same scene again with QPC and the same target.
analysis.diagnostics.guide.gpu.step3: Compare GPUBusy, GPUWait and local dynamic anomalies with the previous run.
analysis.diagnostics.guide.gpu.step4: If nothing improves, restore the setting and test one frame-cap or VSync change only.
analysis.diagnostics.guide.mixed.step1: Fix the scene, route and all settings; record a baseline capture.
analysis.diagnostics.guide.mixed.step2: Change only one CPU-side variable and capture the same scene.
analysis.diagnostics.guide.mixed.step3: Restore it, then change only one GPU-side variable and capture again.
analysis.diagnostics.guide.mixed.step4: Compare both runs; if neither clearly changes, keep the result inconclusive and collect more data.
analysis.diagnostics.guide.memory.step1: Record a baseline in the same scene and note system RAM and target working set in telemetry.
analysis.diagnostics.guide.memory.step2: Close one memory-heavy background app or lower one texture/view-distance setting.
analysis.diagnostics.guide.memory.step3: Capture the same scene again with QPC and complete telemetry.
analysis.diagnostics.guide.memory.step4: Compare RAM, target working set and local anomalies; restore the change if nothing improves.
Fix the game scene and note window mode, VSync, frame cap and refresh rate.
Change only one of: window mode, VSync, or frame cap.
Capture the same scene again and compare displayed-frame ratio and display latency.
If nothing improves, restore the change and test the next single variable.
Enable QPC timebase before starting a new capture.
Keep the telemetry sidecar next to the CSV; do not move or rename it separately.
Enable GPU frame fields (avoid low-overhead mode) if GPU diagnosis is needed.
Capture the same scene for at least 30 seconds, then check time-sync and telemetry coverage.

analysis.diagnostics.why.cpu: LagLens compared how long CPU work took, how long it waited, and how much GPU work was in the same frames. A CPU-heavy pattern can make frames slower, but this comparison cannot prove the CPU caused it.
analysis.diagnostics.why.gpu: LagLens compared GPU work, GPU waiting and CPU frame work. A GPU-heavy pattern can make frames slower, but this comparison cannot prove the GPU caused it, and it does not use total graphics-card load.
analysis.diagnostics.why.mixed: CPU and GPU work were both close to the length of a frame. The data cannot tell which side was the main limit.
analysis.diagnostics.why.memory: System memory use and the game's memory use rose around the slow frames. That can happen by coincidence, so it is not proof that memory caused the slowdown.
analysis.diagnostics.why.presentation: Some frames were not displayed, or display timing changed. That shows a presentation symptom, not its cause.
analysis.diagnostics.why.data_quality: Some fields or timing information are missing or unreliable. LagLens cannot safely connect hardware readings to individual frames.
analysis.diagnostics.why.unknown: No diagnostic rule found enough evidence to point to a cause.
analysis.diagnostics.limit.cpu: CPU busy time is frame-level work, not a specific thread, Windows setting, or proof that the CPU hardware is faulty or too slow.
analysis.diagnostics.limit.gpu: GPU busy time describes the game's GPU work, not total graphics-card load. It does not prove the GPU is faulty or too weak. HAGS can make this less precise.
analysis.diagnostics.limit.mixed: The data supports more than one explanation. Do not treat either side as confirmed.
analysis.diagnostics.limit.memory: System RAM use is not the same as one game's memory use. Growing memory use can be normal caching.
analysis.diagnostics.limit.presentation: A frame that was not displayed does not explain why it was not displayed.
analysis.diagnostics.limit.data_quality: With missing fields or unreliable timing, LagLens cannot safely match hardware readings to individual frames.
analysis.diagnostics.limit.unknown: A link in the data is not proof of cause. More evidence is needed.
analysis.diagnostics.advice.cpu: Try closing one high-CPU background app or lowering one CPU-heavy setting, then capture the same scene again.
analysis.diagnostics.advice.gpu: Try lowering one GPU setting, such as resolution or a graphics preset, or changing the frame cap, then capture the same scene again.
analysis.diagnostics.advice.mixed: Change only a CPU setting or a GPU setting (not both), then capture the same scene again.
analysis.diagnostics.advice.memory: Close one memory-heavy app or lower one texture/view-distance setting, then capture the same scene again.
analysis.diagnostics.advice.presentation: Check window mode, VSync or the frame cap one at a time, then capture the same scene again.
analysis.diagnostics.advice.data_quality: Use QPC timing, keep the telemetry file next to the CSV, and enable GPU frame data if possible.
analysis.diagnostics.advice.unknown: Capture the same route with complete telemetry and GPU data. Do not assign a cause without more evidence.
analysis.diagnostics.code.global_cpu_bot: CPU frame work is the main pressure LagLens can see. This does not prove the CPU itself is too weak.
analysis.diagnostics.code.global_gpu_bot: GPU frame work is the main pressure LagLens can see. This does not prove the GPU is faulty or too weak.
analysis.diagnostics.code.mixed_cpu_gpu_: The data cannot tell whether CPU or GPU work is the main limit.
analysis.diagnostics.code.mixed_frame_pr: CPU and GPU frame work are too close to call. More testing is needed to separate them.
analysis.diagnostics.code.local_stutter_: During this slow moment, CPU work rose more than GPU work. This is a possible link, not a proven cause.
During this slow moment, GPU work rose more than CPU work. This is a possible link, not a proven cause.
During this slow moment, both CPU and GPU work rose. The data does not show which one mattered more.
Display behaviour changed during this slow moment. This is a possible link, not a proven cause.
High RAM use and the game's growing memory use happened around this slow moment. This is a possible link, not a proven cause.
LagLens found a slow moment, but no category had enough evidence to explain it.
analysis.diagnostics.code.global_memory_: High system RAM use and the game's growing memory use happened during frame pressure. This is a possible link, not a proven cause.
analysis.diagnostics.code.displayed_fram: Some captured frames were not displayed. That can make the results less complete.
analysis.diagnostics.code.cpu_fields_una: CPU frame data is missing, so CPU-side comparisons are limited.
analysis.diagnostics.code.gpu_fields_una: GPU frame data is missing (for example, low-overhead capture mode), so GPU-side comparisons are limited.
analysis.diagnostics.code.display_fields: Display data is missing, so LagLens cannot check whether frames reached the screen.
analysis.diagnostics.code.telemetry_unav: No telemetry file was found, so CPU, GPU and RAM samples cannot be tied to frames.
analysis.diagnostics.code.telemetry_time: The timing information is not reliable enough to match hardware samples to frames.
analysis.diagnostics.code.telemetry_samp: There are too few hardware samples for a reliable hardware comparison.
analysis.diagnostics.code.target_cpu_unu: The game's CPU samples are unusable, so per-game CPU use cannot be checked.
analysis.diagnostics.code.insufficient_e: There is not enough evidence to point to a cause.
analysis.report.title: LagLens Diagnostic Report
analysis.report.does_not_tell: What this does not tell you
analysis.report.note: These results are possible links, not confirmed causes. Suggestions are experiments, not instructions.
failure.access_denied: ETW access denied. PresentMon needs administrator privileges (or membership of the "Performance Log Users" group). Restart LagLens as administrator.
failure.session_busy: The PresentMon ETW session is still in use (exit code {exit_code}). Wait a moment and retry.
failure.bad_command: PresentMon rejected the command line. Make sure the selected executable is PresentMon 2.x.
failure.trace_failed: PresentMon could not start its ETW trace session (exit code {exit_code}).
failure.csv_missing: PresentMon exited with code {exit_code} but did not create the CSV. Check that {target} is running and that the captures folder is writable.
failure.no_frames: PresentMon exited with code {exit_code} but captured no frames. Check that {target} is running and presenting frames.
failure.csv_unusable: PresentMon exited with code {exit_code}, but the CSV is not usable: {detail}.
failure.no_data: PresentMon exited successfully but produced no usable frame data.
failure.unknown: PresentMon exited with code {exit_code} without producing frame data.
failure.similar: Also running: {similar}. If the selected process is a launcher, try the other executable.
failure.similar_suggested: Also running: {similar}. Possible renderer: {suggested}. If the selected process is a launcher, try the suggested executable.
quality.truncated: CSV ends with a truncated row (capture may have been interrupted)
quality.bad_fields: {count} row(s) have an unexpected number of fields
quality.na: {count} row(s) have NA frame metrics (frames not captured)
quality.long_frames: {count} frame(s) longer than {threshold} ms (possible stall or lost events)
